feedback.problem:
Consider the following trigonometric equation: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+{50}^{∘})=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}
$$

  

The general solution of this equation can be expressed as

$$
x=a+{360}^{∘}\cdot n,\,x={175}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n,
$$

where $n$ is any integer. Find a possible value of $a$ in the range $({0}^{∘},{90}^{∘}].$

$a=$
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$
feedback.worked_solution:
The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}x+{50}^{∘} & ={135}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n, & \, & \, & x+{50}^{∘} & ={225}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x,$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={135}^{∘}-{50}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n & \, & \, & x & ={225}^{∘}-{50}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n \\ x & ={85}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n & \, & \, & x & ={175}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}\cdot n\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that $a={85}^{∘}.$
